about.title: About Engine Displacement Calculator
about.description: The Engine Displacement Calculator determines total engine displacement based on bore, stroke, and number of cylinders. This fundamental measurement affects power output, fuel consumption, and engine classification. Understanding engine displacement helps with performance modifications, engine swaps, and regulatory compliance for racing classes or emissions requirements.

faq.q: How does engine displacement affect power output?
faq.a: Larger displacement generally produces more power by burning more fuel and air per cycle. However, engine efficiency, compression ratio, valve timing, and breathing characteristics also significantly impact power output. Our displacement calculator helps you understand this fundamental engine measurement.

faq.q: What's the difference between bore and stroke?
faq.a: Bore is the cylinder diameter (width), while stroke is the piston travel distance (height). Larger bore typically favors high RPM power and breathing, while longer stroke provides more torque at lower RPM due to increased leverage on the crankshaft.

faq.q: How do I accurately measure bore and stroke?
faq.a: Bore can be measured with precision calipers or bore gauge inside the cylinder. Stroke is measured as crankshaft throw (distance from center to rod journal) × 2, or by measuring actual piston travel from bottom dead center to top dead center.

faq.q: Why is displacement important for racing classifications?
faq.a: Many racing classes have strict displacement limits to ensure fair competition. Displacement also affects weight penalties, restrictor plate requirements, and class eligibility in various racing series. Our calculator helps verify compliance with racing regulations.

faq.q: What's a good bore-to-stroke ratio for performance?
faq.a: Oversquare engines (bore > stroke) favor high RPM power and breathing, while undersquare engines (stroke > bore) produce more torque. Square engines (bore = stroke) offer balanced characteristics. The right ratio depends on your goals and application.

faq.q: How does displacement relate to fuel consumption?
faq.a: Larger displacement engines typically consume more fuel because they move more air and fuel per cycle. However, modern technology, efficiency improvements, and driving conditions significantly affect actual fuel consumption beyond just displacement.
